hardware: x86_64 Linux container, 4 vCPU, PostgreSQL 17 in Docker; not the target Mac
dataset: 100,000 vehicles (seed) + scripts/sql_history.py: 2,000,000 alerts over 365 days (~1.5 % active) and 150,000 work orders (3,000 active); identical deterministic data for before and after
selection: scripts/sql_workload.py: 3,055 API requests (fleet managers of all 20 tenants, 5 rounds) + 3 planner cycles, ranked by pg_stat_statements total time. The top 3 read queries were optimised; the planner's work-order INSERTs (0.35 ms each) were not.

before.state: old API image, no new indexes

q1_fleet_summary.change: 8 correlated count subqueries -> one pass per table with FILTER aggregates, restricted to active rows; partial index alerts_active_idx, vehicles_tenant_status_idx, work_orders_tenant_status_created_idx
q1_fleet_summary.results_identical: yes, all 20 tenants compared (old vs new SQL on the same data)

q3_work_orders_by_status_page.change: ORDER BY bound to the text alias of work_order_id (no index can supply it) -> qualified columns; index (tenant_id, status, created_at DESC, work_order_id DESC)

q2_planner_open_alerts.change: none to the SQL; the partial index alerts_active_idx is available to it
q2_planner_open_alerts.verdict: NOT improved. The index reads ~22K heap pages instead of 84K, but single-threaded random reads are slower than a parallel full scan when the table is in the OS cache. It returns 22.5K rows each cycle; the real fix is incremental planning (only alerts since the last cycle).
